name: PLESS
aliases: Proscar Long-Term Efficacy and Safety Study
question: Does finasteride reduce symptoms, acute urinary retention, and BPH surgery compared with placebo in men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement?

design.population: 3,040 men with moderate-to-severe urinary symptoms, low maximal urinary flow, and an enlarged prostate on digital rectal examination.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 558; Figure 1, p 559

verdictNote: Prespecified symptom-score endpoint improved in the intention-to-treat analysis; surgery and retention were secondary endpoints.
takeaway: In 3,016 evaluable men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement, finasteride 5 mg daily for four years improved the primary symptom score (mean decrease 2.6 versus 1.0 points; P <0.001) and reduced surgery or acute retention (100/1,513 versus 199/1,503; 51% risk reduction).

reports.label: Four-year randomized report
reports.citation: McConnell JD, Bruskewitz R, Walsh P, et al. "The Effect of Finasteride on the Risk of Acute Urinary Retention and the Need for Surgical Treatment among Men with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *N Engl J Med.* 1998;338(9):557-563. doi:10.1056/NEJM199802263380901

results.measure: Mean decrease in quasi-AUA symptom score (0–34) over 4 years; prespecified stratified intention-to-treat analysis including discontinuations
results.note: Among completers, mean decreases were 3.3 versus 1.3 points (reported difference 2.1; 95% CI 1.6–2.6; P <0.001).
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 558; Results, p 560

results.endpoint: BPH surgery or acute urinary retention
results.measure: First event over 4 years in evaluable men
results.note: Paper reports a 51% risk reduction (95% CI 38–61%) from a time-to-first-event log-rank analysis; the ratio and CI here are inversions of that estimate.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 559–560

results.note: Reported 55% risk reduction (95% CI 41–65%) from time-to-first-event log-rank analysis; 64/1,513 versus 125/1,503 underwent transurethral prostatectomy (49% risk reduction; 95% CI 33–62%).
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 559–560

results.note: Reported 57% risk reduction (95% CI 40–69%) from time-to-first-event log-rank analysis; spontaneous retention: 20/1,513 versus 56/1,503 (62% reduction; 95% CI 40–76%); precipitated retention: 23/1,513 versus 48/1,503 (52% reduction; 95% CI 23–70%). One man could have both types but counted once in total.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 560
Full text, Results and Figure 3, p 561

results.measure: Mean percentage change among 4-year completers in MRI subgroup (157 finasteride; 155 placebo at baseline)
results.note: Volume was measured in 312 men at baseline; four-year MRI measurements were available for 102 finasteride and 85 placebo recipients.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 559; Results and Figure 3, p 561

delivery.label: Open-label extension entry
delivery.value: Of 1,006 original finasteride and 891 placebo recipients completing 4 years, 908 and 785 entered 2 years of open-label finasteride 5 mg daily; complete 6-year outcome data were available for 2,463/3,016 originally evaluable participants, including 770 who discontinued treatment during years 1–6.

delivery.label: Extension analysis and safety ascertainment
delivery.value: Intent-to-treat analyses included originally randomized men treated for at least 1 day; yearly event incidence used life-table methods. An allocation-blinded committee reviewed retention and BPH surgery; extension safety assessments were restricted to serious drug-related adverse experiences.
